merger_description:
Tasmea Limited (ASX: TEA) (**Tasmea**) is an Australian diversified specialist trade‑skill services group. It owns and operates 26 specialised subsidiaries that provide maintenance, shutdown, breakdown and brownfield upgrade services to fixed plant for essential asset owners, across electrical, mechanical, civil and water & fluid trade streams, predominantly for mining and resources, power & renewables and water customers.

JPS Holdings Pty Ltd (**JPS Holdings**) is a Brisbane-headquartered integrated operations and project execution services provider to the Australian oil and gas sector. Through JPS Management & Execution Pty Ltd, it embeds skilled specialists (operators, engineers and project specialists) directly into operators’ teams to deliver operational support, shutdown and campaign execution, specialist project execution, and integrated nitrogen delivery, across onshore, offshore and Floating Liquefied Natural Gas facilities. Through Safe Isolation Australia Pty Ltd, the sole Australian agent for the DBB Saver isolation technology, JPS Holdings enables safe maintenance downstream of passing valves while an oil and gas plant remains online.

Pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement, Tasmea will acquire 100% of the issued share capital of JPS Holdings (together with its subsidiaries) on a cash-free, debt-free basis (the **Acquisition**).

determination_table_content.details:
Tasmea Limited (Tasmea) applied for a notification waiver in respect
of its proposed acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of
JPS Holdings Pty Ltd (JPS Holdings), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Tasmea (ASX: TEA), is an Australian diversified
specialist trade‑skill services group. It owns and operates 26
specialised subsidiaries that provide maintenance, shutdown,
breakdown and brownfield upgrade services to fixed plant for
essential asset owners, across electrical, mechanical, civil and water
& fluid trade streams, predominantly for mining and resources,
power & renewables and water customers.
The target, JPS Holdings is a Brisbane-headquartered integrated
operations and project execution services provider to the Australian
oil and gas sector. Through JPS Management & Execution Pty Ltd, it
embeds skilled specialists (operators, engineers and project
specialists) directly into operators’ teams to deliver operational
support, shutdown and campaign execution, specialist project
execution, and integrated nitrogen delivery, across onshore, offshore
and Floating Liquefied Natural Gas facilities. Through Safe Isolation
Australia Pty Ltd, the sole Australian agent for the DBB Saver
isolation technology, JPS Holdings enables safe maintenance
downstream of passing valves while an oil and gas plant remains
online.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between Tasmea and JPS
Holdings in the supply of plant maintenance trade services
and specialist personnel to oil and gas plants in Australia, as
their respective offerings differ
b. there are alternative suppliers of plant maintenance trade
services and specialist personnel to oil and gas plant
operators in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of plant maintenance trade
services and specialist personnel post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
